chapter_title: Chương 77: 0077【Ngay cả ông bà trong câu lạc bộ cờ cũng biết Trần Quý Lương】

segments.title: Chương 77: 0077【Ngay cả ông bà trong câu lạc bộ cờ cũng biết Trần Quý Lương】
segments.content:
After applying for Peking University's independent recruitment program, Chen Guiliang studied even harder.

If he were to slip up in the college entrance exams and not reach the tier-one cutoff score, he wouldn't be able to get into Peking University through the special admission. That would be too humiliating, probably enough to become a nationwide laughingstock!

Evening.

Xie Yang sauntered back to the dorm after his shower and saw Chen Guiliang wearing headphones with a cassette player in his lap. "What song are you listening to?"

The cassette player was borrowed from Xu Haibo. He planned to buy his own over the weekend, along with a mobile phone.

"English listening comprehension," Chen Guiliang said.

Xie Yang was suddenly speechless and complained, "Damn, do you have to go this hard?"

Chen Guiliang retorted, "If you could get into Peking University just by passing the tier-one cutoff, would you go hard or not?"

"That's true," Xie Yang said, scratching his head.

Li Yulin chuckled. "If it were me, I'd be talking in my sleep in English."

Chen Guiliang's English had always been terrible.

He was a kid from the countryside, after all, and had only started learning it in seventh grade.

His junior high English teacher was a kind-hearted middle-aged woman who often gave Chen Guiliang her old clothes to wear.

But how outrageous was her spoken English?

She actually pronounced "duck" as "duì K," and with a heavy Sichuan Mandarin accent at that!

This led to a long period where Chen Guiliang would think of playing cards whenever he saw a duck.

Although his junior high English teacher wasn't good at teaching, she had relatives and friends who taught in the city, so she could often get practice tests from good schools. She would mimeograph them and toss them to the students, not caring if they finished them, and was even too lazy to go over the tests, just handing out the answer keys directly.

Chen Guiliang didn't do those practice tests either, as there were simply too many of them, coming from the three best junior high schools in the city.

However, Chen Guiliang always went through the questions once while checking the answers.

During the high school entrance exam, 90% of the questions on the English paper were original or similar questions that Chen Guiliang had seen before. The listening comprehension was the exact same material; Chen Guiliang had already finished writing the answers before the audio was even halfway through…

His memory was extraordinary!

After entering high school and university, Chen Guiliang had zero interest in English. He basically never seriously memorized vocabulary, and his listening and speaking skills were atrocious. It took him several tries to pass the CET-4.

Having not had much contact with English for twenty years, he now had to hurry and catch up.

Xu Haibo said, "Xie Sao Bang, you should start working hard too."

"I am working hard."

Xie Yang was a bit impatient and picked up a small mirror to comb his hair.

Liu Zhihong ruthlessly exposed him, "You're working my ass. You've been sleepwalking through morning, noon, and evening self-study sessions."

Xie Yang fell silent.

He really couldn't calm down and study. The closer the college entrance exam got, the more his mind would wander.

But this semester was being monitored tightly, so Xie Yang could no longer go to internet cafes. He could only pass the time by reading novels. Seeing his roommates all studying hard, he would occasionally get serious about studying for a day or two.

Chen Guiliang smiled and said, "Why don't we make a bet. Let's see whose first mock exam score improves more than their final exam score."

"The loser treats the whole dorm to a stir-fry meal!" Xie Yang immediately accepted the challenge, certain of his victory.

Because Chen Guiliang's final exam score was already 6 points above the tier-one cutoff, it would be very difficult to improve significantly.

And Xie Yang?

He did terribly on the last final exam, not even passing the tier-two cutoff. He could raise his score by twenty or thirty points with just a little serious review.

With the bet made, Xie Yang also began to pretend to read a book.

March 1st, evening.

Tao Xue and a chubby girl from her dorm were aimlessly wandering around campus with nothing to do.

She felt very bored.

The senior year was so tightly controlled now that she had no chance to hang out with Chen Guiliang. Even when they did meet, they could only chat for a few minutes.

They left the school and went to the book rental shop.

The chubby girl made a beeline for the romance novel shelf and rented a copy of *Whose Love Isn't Locked*.

Tao Xue, however, casually picked up a copy of *Mengya* magazine and was instantly delighted, "Ah, Chen Guiliang is on the cover!"

The rental shop owner smiled proudly, "Chen Guiliang is a student at this school. He often rents books here. Guo Xiaosi also often rents books from me. You should buy this issue of *Mengya* quickly. It just arrived this afternoon, and there are only three copies left."

"It's selling that well?" Tao Xue was even more pleased than the owner.

The rental shop owner said, "Of course students from our own school have to support him. Usually, it takes about ten days to sell out, but this time it's almost sold out in one afternoon."

A celebrity had emerged from their school, and he had even invited dozens of media outlets, creating such a huge spectacle. Naturally, the students of No. 2 High School paid special attention.

There were always some literature lovers, especially first-year high school girls, who were willing to spend money to buy the magazine in support.

Tao Xue also bought a copy and carried it back to the classroom, pleased as punch.

While the chubby girl was reading her romance novel, Tao Xue glanced around, then turned and asked the boy in the back row who was doing his homework, "Peng Yifan, have you read Chen Guiliang's article?"

"No." The boy continued with his homework.

Tao Xue enthusiastically promoted it, "You should read it. This poem and the preface are so well-written. He even won first prize in the New Concept competition. He's recommended for admission to Peking University!"

Independent recruitment, admission with a lower score—at No. 2 High School, this had already been distorted into "recommended for admission to Peking University."

Hearing the words "recommended for admission to Peking University," the boy finally put down his homework to look at the magazine, and he even savored it repeatedly. "That Chen… Senior Brother Chen, he's really awesome!"

"What do you think? Impressive, right?" Tao Xue said happily.

The boy was at a loss for whether to laugh or cry. "Impressive, he's your grand-nephew, you've said it many times."

After the boy finished reading, Tao Xue approached the next table. "Xue Shiyao, don't you like reading novels? Quick, take a look at these two articles by Chen Guiliang."

The girl glanced over. "It even has annotations, just like the classical texts in the Chinese textbook."

"Impressive, right?" Tao Xue smiled.

"Very impressive. No wonder he's recommended for admission to Peking University," the girl echoed.

At that time, many high school students really did enjoy reading all sorts of essays. The collection of award-winning works from the New Concept competition could sell millions of copies each year.

And that was just the legitimate sales!

By the end of the evening self-study session, thanks to Tao Xue's enthusiastic promotion, that copy of *Mengya* had been read by more than twenty people.

Evening self-study ended.

Zheng Feng and Bian Guanyue still took the same bus, but he didn't get off early, nor would he walk Bian Guanyue into the alley anymore.

Zheng Feng's home was the next stop after Bian Guanyue's.

He took out his keys, opened the door, and went inside. His mother was preparing ingredients for the next day—for their stall selling liangpi, liangmian, and langya potatoes.

His father, exhausted from a long day's work, was lying on the sofa watching TV.

"You're back."

"I'm back."

"There's liangmian on the table, and I boiled an egg for you. Have it as a late-night snack."

Zheng Feng put down his schoolbag and went to eat the liangmian and egg.

His father asked casually, "Is Chen Guiliang in your class?"

Zheng Feng said, "Why do you bring him up?"

"He got recommended for admission to Peking University for writing an essay," his father said.

Zheng Feng was extremely surprised. "You know about it?"

His father said, "This afternoon, while I was prepping vegetables at the restaurant, a few of the kitchen hands were talking about it. They said a student from No. 2 High School was recommended for admission to Peking University, and that he wrote an incredibly fierce article."

"Who did they hear it from?" Zheng Feng asked curiously.

"Last night's Longdu news report."

Chen Guiliang's fame in Longdu City had already evolved to the stage of word-of-mouth.

It started with his appearance on the local television news.

This program mainly reported on the trivial matters of neighborhood gossip, and even frequently showed scenes of cursing and fighting. Occasionally, it would address some long-standing problems, urging the relevant departments to send someone to resolve them.

Its viewership ratings were terrifyingly high!

The common folk just loved watching that kind of content.

Bian Guanyue's home.

Her grandfather was even wearing his reading glasses to read *Mengya*.

The old couple would go play mahjong every few days, playing for ten cents a point—just small stakes for pure entertainment.

That afternoon at the chess and card room, some of their fellow players were discussing the matter. The old folks chattered as if they had witnessed it themselves, as if Chen Guiliang were their own grandson.

Chen Guiliang?

The name sounded very familiar to her grandparents. Wasn't that the boy who took their granddaughter to get her computer fixed?

On their way home, her grandfather passed by a newsstand and asked if there were any newspapers with news about Chen Guiliang.

The vendor tossed him a copy of *Mengya* directly.

"Haven't you finished reading it yet?" her grandmother asked.

Her grandfather said, "I've finished. It's truly well-written. When I was young, I also submitted manuscripts to the factory newspaper, and they even published two of my modern poems."

"That was decades ago, and you're bringing it up again. My ears are growing calluses," her grandmother complained.

Her grandfather pointed at *Mengya* and said, "A poem like this, I could never write it. He can definitely be called a man of letters."

"Who's talking to you about that?" Her grandmother started to get to the main point. "Is Guan Guan in a puppy love relationship with him? It'll affect her studies! The more talented they are, the better they are at coaxing girls. I'm afraid Guan Guan has been completely charmed by him."

Her grandfather chuckled. "You seem to have personal experience."

"You're not worried at all," her grandmother said helplessly.

Her grandfather said, "As long as he's not a bad student, it's fine. Puppy love is just puppy love."

The sound of a key turning in the lock was heard.

Her grandfather deftly stuffed *Mengya* under the sofa cushion.

Her grandmother went to the kitchen to bring Bian Guanyue a late-night snack, asking casually, "Is it true that a student from your school was recommended for admission to Peking University?"

"Yes, there is one."

Bian Guanyue's expression was a little unnatural. Fearing her grandparents would see through something, she quickly sat down and lowered her head to eat the sweet dumplings.

The old couple exchanged a look, now completely certain.

"Meow, meow~~"

The kitten slipped under the table and circled around Bian Guanyue's feet, trying to climb up her pant leg.

So, Bian Guanyue pretended to be playing with the cat.

After finishing the bowl of sweet dumplings, Bian Guanyue quickly fled back to her bedroom. Lying on her bed, she opened her pencil case and took out that broken stone of Qin Shi Huang's.

"He's going to Peking University. I have to work hard too and try to get into a good university in Beijing!"

Bian Guanyue carefully put the broken stone away, turned on her desk lamp, and started working on her test papers.

The two articles by Chen Guiliang published in this issue of *Mengya* caused a huge stir among high school students across the country.

People who haven't lived through that era would find it hard to imagine the influence of *Mengya* among teenagers. Even some students who weren't fond of literature would, out of boredom, occasionally pick up a classmate's copy of *Mengya* and flip through it.

If a particular article was especially brilliant, there would be spontaneous promoters like Tao Xue, who would actively publicize it to other classmates.

Did "A Journey to the Sea of Stars" have a high barrier to entry as a piece of classical poetry?

*For Sadness Does Not Last*, which had just finished its serialization a while ago, was what truly had a high barrier to entry. The author used almost every technique he could think of, employing an extremely deterring writing style, to tell a very boring story.

Even this kind of purely technique-flexing, pure-literature novel could get countless high school students to follow it issue after issue, and for more than half a year at that… The post-2000s generation, keen on scrolling through TikTok, would probably find it hard to understand.

In the first five years of the 21st century, as long as your writing was good, you would not lack young people to admire you.

On the very day the magazine was released, some students took "A Journey to the Sea of Stars" to consult their Chinese teachers.

Consulting was a pretense; showing off was the real intention.

It was unclear what they were showing off about.

"Teacher, this is Chen Guiliang's award-winning essay. He was even recommended for admission to Peking University because of this article."

"Let me have a look."

Across the country, more than one or two Chinese teachers told their students in class, "This article is very well-written, and the author has already been recommended for admission to Peking University. Today, we'll analyze it and see why it's so good. You can't just learn this; you need to accumulate knowledge in your daily life… Also, the author's other article, which questions the errors in the annotations of the 'Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng,' I find it very reasonable as well. But when you take your exams, you must still follow the textbook…"

Meanwhile, the reports from those dozens of media outlets were also published one after another.

The focus varied wildly: some discussed the fairness of student recruitment, some mocked Chen Guiliang for his arrogance, some wrote about the "one hundred million small goal" as a joke, and some praised Chen Guiliang profusely without reservation.

There were also some who demanded that the Chinese textbook be corrected, and this kind of report surprisingly sparked a heated discussion.

As Chen Guiliang was about to take his first mock exam, Professor Liu Yongxiang from East China Normal University was the first to enter the fray.

He had written an article pointing out the textbook error two years prior, but it hadn't received any attention. Now was the perfect opportunity to bring it up again.

Professor Liu also stated in an interview, "Although student Chen Guiliang is still in high school, he has already shown the potential for academic research. If he comes to East China Normal University for his master's or doctorate in the future, I would be very willing to be his advisor…"
